sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real decision, by when, and which numbers frame it?
criteria: Restates the decision as what to offer within your authority in 10 days, and how to protect the refresh either way
Derives the gap between the offer and current pay ($160k, 44%) and between the offer and the band maximum ($120k)
Identifies key-person risk on the refresh as a problem to fix whatever Maya decides
States at least one thing out of scope or unknown

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Puts Maya first, with her stated reason (scope and on-call) ahead of money
Includes HR, your manager, Ravi and the on-call rotation, each with a distinct want
Includes the two other principals as an internal-equity stake
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real options, and how does each do on the 10-day deadline, fairness and the refresh?
criteria: Includes letting her go well as an option
Shows that matching $520k can't be promised in 10 days and breaks the band
Rejects promising a committee outcome or a future promotion to close the decision
Compares options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you offer, what do you give up, and what would make you change course?
criteria: Leads with the role (BEC lead, off on-call) and adds cash and equity within policy
Says plainly that the offer does not match $520k, and by how much ($45k in year one)
Names what is given up, including Maya on the refresh and the external lead search
Gives a dated revisit with measurable triggers

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does keeping her cost, and what does losing her cost, over the same horizon?
criteria: Prices the counter over 3 years ($270k) and a cash match over 3 years ($480k)
Prices losing her: agency fee, BEC launch delay ($250k a month) and the refresh precedent ($1.1M ARR)
Shows how converting the lead role to a senior hire funds the counter
Labels all compensation figures as assumed

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns what after Maya's role changes?
criteria: Makes Ravi the owner of this refresh, with Maya as reviewer
Keeps the on-call rotation at 4 without Maya
Gives Maya a defined BEC remit with a launch milestone

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens in the next 10 days and the next 10 weeks?
criteria: Has a stay conversation in the first days, before making the offer
Gets HR approval for the offer inside the 10-day window
Completes the runbook and a dry run before the refresh is due
Includes a revisit at 6 months

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong with fairness, policy and the refresh?
criteria: Keeps the offer within policy and doesn't promise a committee outcome
Flags the internal-equity effect on the two other principals to HR
Avoids teaching the team that an outside offer is the way to get scope or pay
Has a plan for the refresh if Maya leaves anyway

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know it worked, and what would show it is causing harm?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks the refresh on time with customer-reported misses as the guard
Tracks the on-call load on the rest of the team
Tracks Maya's BEC milestones, not just whether she stayed

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and what stays private?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences
Keeps the outside offer private from the team
Tells your manager the cost of both outcomes
Sets a cadence for following up with Maya after she decides
